title: Finite strict-to-path iterated pullback comparison
statement: Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, weak homotopy equivalences and internal functor simplicial sets as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $B,E$ be Kan complexes and let $s,t:E\to B$ be Kan fibrations, meaning maps with the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. Put $P_1=E$ and $P_k=P_{k-1}\times_B E$ by matching the last endpoint to $s$. Put $H_1=E$ and $H_k=H_{k-1}\times^h_B E$ using the same endpoint convention, where $U\times^h_B V=U\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B}V$. Then the maps $c_k:P_k\to H_k$ inserting constant paths at all matched vertices are weak homotopy equivalences, and each $c_k$ commutes strictly with the endpoint map given by the last $E$ coordinate. Every $H_k$ is Kan. No nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed, and $k$ ranges over positive integers.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 3.4.0.7 (0329), together with Proposition 3.4.0.9 (032B), applied inductively to the finite endpoint-matched tower; the finite induction and strict endpoint compatibility are expanded here.

proof.text: Write $r_j:P_j\to B$ and $h_j:H_j\to B$ for $t$ on the last $E$ coordinate. Construct $c_j$ recursively, keeping all $E$ coordinates. Set $c_1=1_E$. Given $c_j$ with $h_jc_j=r_j$, send an $n$-simplex $(p,e)$ of $P_{j+1}$ to $(c_j(p),\operatorname{const}(r_j(p)),e)$ of $H_{j+1}$. Here the constant path on an $n$-simplex $b:\Delta^n\to B$ is the map $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to\Delta^n\xrightarrow{b}B$. Its two endpoint restrictions are both $b$. Thus $h_jc_j(p)=r_j(p)=s(e)$ verifies both pullback equations. Precomposition in $\Delta^n$ commutes with this projection, so the displayed construction is simplicial by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Its last coordinate is $e$, hence $h_{j+1}c_{j+1}(p,e)=t(e)=r_{j+1}(p,e)$. This constructs all the stated constant-path maps and proves the strict endpoint identity by induction, independently of their weak equivalence.

source.place: Construction 3.4.0.3: degreewise path pullback and its constant-path map; recursive coordinate verification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-iterated-pullback-fibrancy] with the given Kan complexes $E,B$ and the two given Kan fibrations $s,t$. Its recursively defined tower and endpoint maps are exactly $P_j$ and $r_j$. Therefore every $P_j$ is Kan (and $r_j$ is a Kan fibration). In particular the strict tower supplies Kan inputs for each application of the binary comparison below.

source.place: Subsection 3.1.1, Remarks 3.1.1.6, 3.1.1.10 and 3.1.1.11, packaged by the existing finite-tower node.

proof.text: Induct on positive $j$ for the simultaneous claim that $H_j$ is Kan and $c_j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. For $j=1$, $H_1=E$ is Kan by hypothesis and $c_1=1_E$ induces identity maps on components and all based homotopy groups. Fix $j\geq1$ and assume this claim for $j$; the next two steps establish it for $j+1$.

source.place: Finite induction set-up and identity base case; agent expansion.

proof.text: Put $J_{j+1}=P_j\times_{B,r_j,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B,s}E$. The three inputs $P_j,E,B$ are Kan by step 2 and the hypotheses. Since $s:E\to B$ is a Kan fibration, [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] gives a weak homotopy equivalence $a_{j+1}:P_{j+1}\to J_{j+1}$ with formula $(p,e)\mapsto(p,\operatorname{const}(r_j(p)),e)$, and also says $J_{j+1}$ is Kan. Apply the Kan assertion of that same node to $h_j:H_j\to B$ and $s:E\to B$. The induction hypothesis gives that $H_j$ is Kan, so it follows that $H_{j+1}$ is Kan. This last application uses no fibration hypothesis on $h_j$.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.7 and the Kan path-model assertion of the existing binary comparison node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to the two spans $P_j\xrightarrow{r_j}B\xleftarrow{s}E$ and $H_j\xrightarrow{h_j}B\xleftarrow{s}E$, with vertical maps $c_j,1_E,1_B$. All their objects are Kan by step 2, the induction hypothesis and the original hypotheses. Their vertical maps are weak homotopy equivalences by the induction hypothesis and the identity case, and the required squares commute strictly by step 1. The node therefore gives a weak homotopy equivalence $b_{j+1}:J_{j+1}\to H_{j+1}$ sending $(p,\gamma,e)$ to $(c_j(p),\gamma,e)$. Composing with $a_{j+1}$ yields $(p,e)\mapsto(c_j(p),\operatorname{const}(r_j(p)),e)$, exactly $c_{j+1}$ as constructed in step 1. By the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the map on components of a composite is the composite of the two bijections, and its map on the homotopy group at a source basepoint is the composite of the two isomorphisms, using the image basepoint for the second. Thus $c_{j+1}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Together with step 4 this closes the induction. Step 1 already proves strict endpoint preservation in every degree. The argument requires no vertices to be chosen in $E$ or $B$, so it also covers empty complexes.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.9, applied to the endpoint-preserving inductive comparison; identification of the composite and completion of the finite induction.
